lesson.title: Inversion Gym
lesson.subtitle: vandaag, morgen, hier, daar — front it and invert it

hook.title: Front It, Invert It
hook.content: The more fronted words you meet, the more the same inversion appears. Vandaag ga ik, morgen komt zij, hier werk ik, daar werkt hij. One rule, four surfaces.

pattern.title: The subject follows the verb
pattern.content: After a fronted element, the subject follows the finite verb. The verb does not change its tense or its person; only the order changes.
pattern.trap_note: Inversion is not a question marker by itself. Vandaag werk ik is a statement even though the verb comes before the subject.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Inversion Gym):
exercises.target_answer: vandaag, de morgen, gaan, komen, werken, hier
exercises.meaning: today, tomorrow; morning, to go, to come, to work, here
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Inversion Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.
“Vandaag ga ik.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Inversion Gym”.

cues: The pattern: The subject follows the verb
exercises.explanation: “Morgen komt zij.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — The subject follows the verb.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Inversion is not a question marker by itself. Vandaag werk ik is a statement even though the verb comes before the subject.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Hier werk ik.” is word-for-word “Here work I.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: The subject follows the verb.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.explanation: “Daar werkt hij.” reuses only material taught in “Inversion Gym” — The subject follows the verb.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Daar werkt hij.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising The subject follows the verb.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “Today we are here.”
twist.explanation: Zijn is the finite verb, so it takes second place and wij follows.

summary.outcome: Invert subject and finite verb after any fronted element.
summary.takeaway: Inversion is the normal consequence of V2, not an emergency manoeuvre.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Modals & the Final Infinitive.

vandaag.etymology_derivation: van ('of') + dag ('day'): on the day of today.

morgen.etymology_derivation: English morrow and Dutch morgen are the same word.

gaan.etymology_derivation: The same verb as English go, with the old g still pronounced.

komen.etymology_derivation: English come and Dutch komen are the same verb; the vowel differs.

werken.etymology_derivation: English work and Dutch werken are the same verb.

hier.etymology_derivation: The same place word as English here.
